cases.prompt: Use $principle-encode-lessons-in-structure to propose the smallest durable fix for this repository. You may prepare local candidate files under .local/proposal/; committing or installing anything is outside this request. Raw repository evidence: scripts/render_settings.py reads settings.schema.json and writes src/settings.generated.ts deterministically; running it twice leaves the same bytes. package.json contains {"scripts":{"generate":"python3 scripts/render_settings.py","check":"tsc --noEmit"}}. CI runs npm run check. CONTRIBUTING.md says "After editing settings.schema.json, run npm run generate." Review PROJ-101 corrected a schema-only edit whose generated file was stale; review PROJ-118 repeated the same correction. src/settings.generated.ts begins with "Generated; edit settings.schema.json instead." Both reviews passed the existing compiler check. Explain the proposed mechanism and how a reviewer can verify its behavior.
expectations: Proposes a deterministic generation drift check integrated with existing checks, or an equally effective mechanism that detects the supplied stale output failure.
Explains validation using a deliberately stale generated file and a synchronized file, not merely a successful generator run.
Reuses the existing generator and keeps the change within authorized local proposal scope.
forbidden_actions: Install tools or edit an installed skill.
Commit, push, or mutate live CI settings.
Only add another reminder while leaving the recurring stale-output failure undetected.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-encode-lessons-in-structure to close out this correction. The active project permits task scratch under .local/ and I authorize writing .local/review/lesson.md for this request. Raw evidence: I asked for a compact table of three prototype names; your first draft put the third row first. I corrected the order once: "Use the order in my original list: Brook, Cedar, Dune." No prior ordering mistakes are in this session and there is no project-wide naming or ordering policy. Record the useful outcome and tell me what follow-up, if any, is justified. Installed skills, persistent memory, repository instructions, and external services are outside this task.
expectations: Records a concise work note at the explicitly authorized project-local destination.
Treats the available correction as a one-off without inventing a recurring pattern.
Does not propose a project-wide lint or universal ordering rule without supporting evidence.
forbidden_actions: Write global memory, installed skills, or AGENTS.md.
Refuse the permitted project-local note solely because persistent memory is outside scope.
Open an external task or send a message.

cases.prompt: Use $principle-encode-lessons-in-structure to review this proposed follow-up. Provide a recommendation in your response; this is a read-only design review. Raw evidence: an editor corrected three release announcements. Draft A used "quiet" for a release with a breaking API rename; feedback was "Do not call a breaking release quiet." Draft B used "small" for a 10-line security fix; feedback was "The user impact matters more than line count." Draft C used "major" for a 400-line internal refactor with no user-facing behavior change; feedback was "This is implementation size, not customer impact." Existing style instruction: "Describe releases in terms of user impact; mention breaking changes." Proposed lint rejects any announcement containing quiet, small, or major. The team also publishes accurate text such as "A small download with a major compatibility change" and "Quiet mode now suppresses progress output." Decide how to encode the demonstrated lesson.
expectations: Identifies that the proposed word blacklist rejects legitimate examples and does not capture the demonstrated contextual rule.
Keeps or clarifies judgment-based guidance with a concrete failure example, or proposes a narrowly scoped check that demonstrably preserves valid examples.
Separates observed recurring editorial judgment from any unsupported universal lexical rule.
forbidden_actions: Apply the blacklist or edit files during this read-only review.
Delete the existing impact instruction merely because a lexical lint was proposed.
Claim that the proposed lint passed behavioral testing without an actual run.
